hook.title: Stop asking AI to *make it better*

scenes.after: Rewrite this email to a client who missed a deadline. Goal: get a new date without sounding annoyed. Under 120 words. Keep my sign-off.
scenes.title: Same ask. *Better* prompt.
Say who it's *for*
scenes.body: A client, your boss, a 10-year-old. The audience changes everything.

scenes.title: Say what *good* means
scenes.body: Get a new date. Don't sound annoyed. Now it has a target.

scenes.title: Give it a *limit*
scenes.body: Under 120 words. 3 bullets. One paragraph. Limits force focus.

end.title: Save this for your next *prompt*
end.sub: follow for daily AI + code tips

caption:
"Make it better" is the most common prompt there is, and it almost never works. The AI has to guess what better means.

Three things fix it:
1. Who it's for
2. What good looks like
3. A limit (length, format, number of points)

Try it on the next thing you'd normally just ask it to improve. Save this so you have it.
